description: Committee recommends $1 million loan to TCU Place.
Funds new theatre sound system over 10 years.
Loan at 4.153% interest, $30,600 quarterly payments.

chips.text: Loan helps TCU Place maintain $3.8 million reserves for flexibility.

description: Recommends $3.8 million loan for 2950 Lorne Avenue works yard.
Loan repaid through the utility.
Council should approve interim parking lot at 52 - 25th Street East.
Upgrades would cost $150,000 from capital project P.01420.
Lot could generate $50,000 net revenue annually.

chips.text: Addresses off-street parking demand in the 25th Street East area.

description: City will audit group purchasing organizations for value.
Audit will review city procurement processes.

chips.text: Councillor hopes audit finds financial savings for the city.
Auditor committed to inform committee if GPOs withhold necessary information.

description: Committee recommends land acquisition for College Drive BRT.
Total $848,700, within existing project budget.

chips.text: St. Thomas More and St. Andrew's Colleges sell 9,092 sq ft for $848,700.

description: Approves a 2-year, 1-month lease for a Coming Home Centre.
Provides culturally appropriate space for Indigenous women, girls, two-spirits.
Annual cost is $69,000, funded by capital project.

chips.text: Councillors questioned if city should host, suggesting partnerships.
Parking stalls are for community members using the centre.
Administration will report on centre's benefits for 2028-2029 budget.

description: City will lease 17.5 acres in Aspen Ridge.
Lease expected to generate $1 million annually.
This approach prioritizes long-term financial sustainability.

chips.text: Councillor praised 'outside the box' thinking for long-term financial sustainability.
City adopts land lease model for revenue, moving from traditional land sales.

description: Five reports provided information to Council.
Saskatoon Land generated $96 million in 2025 sales.
Net earnings for 2025 were $28.8 million.
Land sales supported housing for unhoused populations.
City plans future land releases to meet housing demand.

chips.text: Councillor Tower concerned about future land supply and housing affordability.
Councillor sought ways to accelerate land concept plan approvals.
Mayor asked for net profit margin comparison to previous years.
Land acquired for winter warming and supportive housing for unhoused.

description: City Auditor's 2025 annual report details office activities.
Report includes whistleblower hotline usage information.

chips.text: City Auditor clarified whistleblower reports include HR-related employee performance issues.
City employees use the whistleblower complaint line.

description: City administration updated finance committee on outstanding tasks and timelines.
City to explore strengthening municipal service audit function.
Administration to report on Chamber's improvement recommendations.

chips.text: Mayor clarified administration does not have oversight of the independent city auditor.
Saskatoon taxpayers are affected by how public money is spent and programs delivered.
Chamber of Commerce presented research and recommendations to strengthen city's audit function.

speakers.name: Jason Aebig
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Stengthening Municipal Service Audit at CoS
said: Strengthen municipal service audit for timely budget information.
Saskatoon's auditor office is under-resourced and lacks independent oversight.
Implement dedicated audit committee, increase staff, and revive whistleblower program.

description: Saskatoon approved a Land Matter.
